title: First Real Footage of a Mars Rover Landing
description: Watch the Perseverance rover's historic touchdown captured by its own cameras. Every moment from entry to surface is shown in real time.

shots.narration: The rover entered Mars’ atmosphere at twenty thousand kilometres per hour, captured by a downward‑facing camera.
A twenty‑one point five metre parachute unfurled supersonically, its pattern spelling Dare Mighty Things in binary.
The downward camera shows the rover descending, the red landscape rushing past in a blur.
The skycrane hovered, lowering the one‑ton rover on seven point six metre cables.
Below, Jezero Crater spreads out, the ancient lakebed where rivers flowed billions of years ago.
The skycrane released the rover, which touched the surface as the descent stage rockets away.
The rover stands on the dusty plain, instruments ready to explore the ancient shoreline.
The rover’s wheels settle, dust swirling, as the descent stage retreats to crash far away.
Radio signals took eleven minutes to reach Earth, so the landing was complete before anyone heard it.
